title: Static checks for agent-authored Db2 13 for z/OS DDL scripts
authority: Official IBM Db2 13 for z/OS documentation only. Each rule cites source IDs from kb/data/db2z13-create-ddl.json.

severity_policy.error: Violates a documented Db2 13 for z/OS rule as encoded here. Fix before delivery.
severity_policy.unsupported: Outside the clause subset this checker models, or not Db2 13 for z/OS syntax. The script fails unless --allow-unsupported is given; resolve it against IBM documentation before claiming the SQL is valid.
severity_policy.warning: Environment-dependent, deprecated or likely-wrong usage. Review it and record the decision.
severity_policy.notice: Information a reviewer needs, such as statements this checker did not examine.

scope: Structural and cross-statement checks for STOGROUP, DATABASE, [LOB] TABLESPACE, TABLE, AUXILIARY TABLE and INDEX. Other statements are recognized for ordering and reported as not checked. Passing these checks does not prove that Db2 accepts the SQL; that requires execution on a recorded subsystem.

rules.summary: The statement could not be read with the modeled grammar.
The statement verb is not a recognized Db2 SQL statement for this checker.
The last statement has no outer terminator; SPUFI/DSNTEP2-style processors may not submit it.
A trigger or procedure body with BEGIN ... END was split by the outer terminator. SQL PL bodies need an alternate outer terminator (for example --#SET TERMINATOR @).
An unresolved {{TOKEN}} template placeholder. Render templates before delivery or execution; use --allow-placeholders only to check a template.
A source line exceeds the requested --max-line record width.
A clause from another SQL dialect (Db2 LUW, Oracle, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server) that is not in the Db2 13 for z/OS diagram.
A data type name that is not in the Db2 13 for z/OS built-in-type diagram and was not created as a distinct type.
IF NOT EXISTS is not in the Db2 13 for z/OS CREATE diagrams.
IF EXISTS is not in the Db2 13 for z/OS DROP diagram.
CREATE OR REPLACE is supported only for routines/triggers, not for tables, table spaces, indexes, databases, storage groups, views, sequences or aliases.
A bare NULL column attribute. Db2 13 for z/OS columns are nullable when NOT NULL is omitted; NULL is only a DEFAULT value.
ON UPDATE referential actions do not exist in Db2 13 for z/OS; the references clause has only ON DELETE.
An ON DELETE action other than RESTRICT, NO ACTION, CASCADE or SET NULL.
A partial index predicate. Db2 13 for z/OS has only UNIQUE WHERE NOT NULL.
A token where the modeled diagram expects a clause. It may be invalid, or valid syntax that this checker does not model yet.
XML type modifiers are recognized but not checked.
The same clause is specified more than once; the diagrams state that a clause must not be repeated.
ALTER TABLE can omit ADD only before a unique or referential constraint that is its first clause; a check constraint or any later constraint needs ADD.
CREATE LARGE TABLESPACE is tolerated only for compatibility; use DSSIZE.
A deprecated or removed table-space option outside the current UTS model.
ENDING AT in CREATE INDEX is the deprecated index-controlled partitioning form.

An identifier is longer than the documented limit: 8 bytes for databases, table spaces and buffer pools; 128 bytes for tables, indexes, constraints, schemas and storage groups; 30 bytes for columns unless TABLE_COLUMN_NAME_EXPANSION is on (then 128).
A column name longer than 30 bytes relies on TABLE_COLUMN_NAME_EXPANSION, which the profile records as on. IBM documents restrictions on such names.
A database or table-space name must start with a letter and must not include special characters.

A database or table-space name contains an underscore or national extender ($, #, @). IBM says these names must not include special characters; confirm the character is accepted on the target subsystem.
Database names that start with DSNDB, or use the implicit DSN plus five digits pattern, are reserved.
A buffer-pool name outside BP0-BP49, BP8K0-BP8K9, BP16K0-BP16K9, BP32K and BP32K1-BP32K9.
An object with the same name is created twice in the script without an intervening DROP.
A constraint name is repeated within one table.
An object is referenced before the statement that creates it.
An object is referenced but neither created in the script nor declared with --assume. It must already exist on the target subsystem.
A table space without IN is created in DSNDB04; an IN db.ts reference without the database resolves to DSNDB04.
SEGSIZE must be a multiple of 4 in the range 4-64.
MAXPARTITIONS must be 1-4096 and no larger than the documented maximum for the DSSIZE and page size.
NUMPARTS must be 1-4096; with MAXPARTITIONS it must not exceed MAXPARTITIONS.
PBG and absolute-numbering PBR DSSIZE must be a power of two 1-256 G; relative-numbering PBR DSSIZE must be 1-1024 G.
DSSIZE above 4 G requires a DFSMS data class with extended format and extended addressability.
FREEPAGE must be 0-255, PCTFREE 0-99, FOR UPDATE -1 to 99, and PCTFREE plus FOR UPDATE at most 99.
MAXROWS must be 1-255.
Base table spaces accept LOCKSIZE ANY, TABLESPACE, PAGE or ROW; LOB table spaces accept ANY or LOB.
With LOCKSIZE TABLESPACE, LOCKMAX must be omitted or 0.
PAGENUM and PARTITION clauses belong to the partition-by-range specification (NUMPARTS without MAXPARTITIONS).
A PARTITION clause number must be unique and between 1 and NUMPARTS.
A partition-by-growth table space cannot use USING VCAT.
An explicit base table space is created but no table is placed in it.
A column has no data type and is not one of the generated timestamp forms that infer a type.
A column clause is specified more than once in one column definition.
A column name is repeated in one table.
A table can have at most 750 columns, or 749 if it is a dependent table.
A length, precision, or scale outside the built-in-type limits.

DEFAULT accepts a constant, USER, SESSION_USER, CURRENT SQLID, NULL, or a cast function for a distinct type. CURRENT TIMESTAMP/DATE and expressions are not DEFAULT values; a value-less WITH DEFAULT on a datetime column yields the current value.
DEFAULT must not be specified for identity, ROWID, row-change timestamp, row-begin, row-end, transaction-start-ID or XML columns.
A table can have at most one identity column, and its type must be an exact numeric with scale zero.
A table can have at most one row-change timestamp, row-begin, row-end and transaction-start-ID column.
ROWID, row-change timestamp, row-begin, row-end and transaction-start-ID columns must be NOT NULL where IBM requires it.
A key, period or partitioning column does not identify a column of the table.
Primary-key and unique-key columns must be defined NOT NULL.
Primary/unique keys cannot include LOB, ROWID, XML or row-change timestamp columns; foreign keys additionally exclude DECFLOAT.
A table can have only one primary key.
A primary, unique, foreign or partitioning key can have at most 64 columns, with no column repeated.
Primary/unique key length must not exceed 2000 - n - 2m - 3d bytes.
The sum of foreign-key column length attributes must not exceed 255 minus the number of nullable columns.
In an ordinary CREATE TABLE the parent table must already exist, so a table cannot reference itself; add a self-referencing constraint with ALTER TABLE.
A referential constraint whose parent is its own table must have the delete rule CASCADE or NO ACTION. Under CURRENT RULES 'DB2' an omitted rule defaults to RESTRICT, which is rejected.

Relationships whose parents are the same table, or are linked by cascading deletes (one cascades to the other, or a third table cascades to both), must have the same delete rule, and it must not be SET NULL.

A foreign key added by ALTER TABLE must not delete-connect a table to itself: it cannot close a cycle whose other relationships are all CASCADE, and it cannot be CASCADE when its parent is already delete-connected to its dependent.
ALTER TABLE ... ADD FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE SET NULL is not allowed when a nullable foreign-key column is in the key of a partitioning index.
ALTER TABLE ... ADD PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE needs an existing unique index with the same columns in the same order; only a table in an implicitly created table space gets one from Db2.

Some tables accept only some ALTER TABLE clauses: a catalog table only DATA CAPTURE CHANGES, an accelerator-only table only ADD or DROP RESTRICT ON DROP, an auxiliary table only APPEND, and a materialized query table only AUDIT, DATA CAPTURE, RESTRICT ON DROP and its partition, query and key-label clauses.
The parent key must match the primary key or a unique key of the parent table, in the same column order. An omitted column list requires a parent primary key.
A foreign key must have the same number of columns as its parent key.
Apart from names, defaults, nullability and checks, each foreign-key column must have the same description (type, length, scale, subtype/CCSID) as its parent-key column.
ON DELETE SET NULL requires at least one nullable foreign-key column.
The parent table must have a unique index for its parent key when the foreign key is created. An explicit table space parent needs its enforcing index created first.
PERIOD BUSINESS_TIME must appear in both the FOREIGN KEY and REFERENCES lists, and requires ON DELETE RESTRICT.
A CHECK constraint can be at most 3800 bytes.
LOGGED/NOT LOGGED, COMPRESS, DSSIZE, BUFFERPOOL, MEMBER CLUSTER, TRACKMOD and PAGENUM on CREATE TABLE apply only to an implicitly created table space.
DATA CAPTURE CHANGES must not be specified for a table in a table space that specifies NOT LOGGED.
IN db.ts must name an existing explicit base table space in that database that does not already contain a table and is not a LOB table space.
A table in a PBR table space needs PARTITION BY RANGE with one element per table-space partition; a PBG table space cannot hold a range-partitioned table.
Partitioning columns must not exceed 64 columns or 255 - n bytes.
BUSINESS_TIME columns must be DATE or TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL and not generated; SYSTEM_TIME must name the row-begin and row-end columns.
At the end of the script a table in an explicit table space still lacks a required enforcing unique index (primary key, unique key, or ROWID GENERATED BY DEFAULT). Db2 marks such a table unavailable.

A LOB column of a table in an explicit table space under CURRENT RULES DB2 needs a LOB table space, auxiliary table and auxiliary index (per partition for PBR). Without them the table definition is incomplete.
The estimated maximum record length exceeds the page-size limit (4056/8138/16330/32714 bytes without EDITPROC). This is an estimate from declared types.
The cast-function form of DEFAULT can be used only with a column defined as a distinct type.
LIKE, AS ... WITH NO DATA and MQT definitions derive columns from other objects; their columns are not checked.
An auxiliary table must be in an existing LOB table space in the base table's database, and must store an existing LOB column; one auxiliary table per column (per partition).
An index key or INCLUDE column does not identify a column of the table.
An index can have at most 64 columns including INCLUDE columns, with no column repeated.
LOB columns cannot be index keys; an XML column needs XMLPATTERN; VARBINARY cannot be in a PADDED index.
The sum of key column length attributes exceeds 2000 - n (padded) or 2000 - n - 2m - 3d (not padded) for a nonpartitioning index, or the 255-byte formulas for a partitioning index.
INCLUDE requires UNIQUE and is not allowed for expression, XML or auxiliary indexes.
INCLUDE columns must differ from the key columns and from each other, and cannot be LOB or DECFLOAT.
PARTITIONED and index PARTITION BY RANGE require a table in a partition-by-range table space; they are invalid on PBG.
A UNIQUE partitioned secondary index must contain all partitioning columns in its key (not in INCLUDE).
A table can have one clustering index, and CLUSTER cannot be used with a key expression or XMLPATTERN.
DESC cannot be used with key expressions; RANDOM cannot be used with a varying-length key in a NOT PADDED index or with TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE/DECFLOAT keys.
Index FREEPAGE must be 0-255 and PCTFREE 0-99.
An index on an auxiliary table has no column list, and an auxiliary table can have only one index.
Padding is omitted on an index with varying-length keys; the PADIX subsystem parameter supplies the default. The key-length limit was checked for both outcomes.
An index that enforces a primary/unique key cannot be dropped while the constraint exists.
The script uses syntax or behavior that IBM gates at a higher APPLCOMPAT level than the profile records. Db2 returns an error such as SQLCODE -4743 or keeps the previous behavior.
The script needs a Db2 13 function level higher than the activated level in the profile.
The profile's APPLCOMPAT is higher than its activated function level, or a level is not a valid V10R1/V11R1/V12R1Mnnn/V13R1Mnnn value.
The minimum APPLCOMPAT and function level that the gated syntax in this script needs. Record the real values in the profile to check them.
Synonyms and hash-organized tables cannot be created at APPLCOMPAT V12R1M504 or higher (the current UTS baseline); IBM announces removal at V13R1M511.
An omitted clause whose default depends on APPLCOMPAT, such as MAXPARTITIONS (254 at V13R1M500 or higher, 256 at V12R1M504-V13R1M100).
A feature IBM lists as deprecated in Db2 13, such as absolute page numbering for PBR table spaces or external SQL procedures.
When the base table is in a partitioned (PBG or PBR) table space, CREATE AUXILIARY TABLE needs PART n, one auxiliary table per partition and LOB column; PART is not allowed otherwise.
PRIQTY must be a positive integer or -1; SECQTY must be a positive integer, 0 or -1.
FOR SORT and FOR DGTT apply only to partition-by-growth table spaces in a work file database.
Statements recognized for ordering only. Their syntax and semantics were not checked.
